questions.question: Which two groups dominated Mesopotamia from the beginning of recorded history to the fall of Babylon in 539 BC?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the Sumerians and Akkadians dominated Mesopotamia from the beginning of recorded history to the fall of Babylon in 539 BC.
Incorrect. The Romans and Parthians battled over Mesopotamia much later, around 150 BC onward.
Incorrect. Assyria and Babylonia were polarized in the early second millennium BC, but they are not the two groups said to dominate from the beginning of recorded history.
Incorrect. The Persians and Greeks conquered Mesopotamia later, after 539 BC.

questions.question: Which empire conquered Mesopotamia in 539 BC?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that in 539 BC, Mesopotamia was conquered by the Achaemenid Empire under Cyrus the Great.
Incorrect. The Roman Empire came into conflict with Parthians over Mesopotamia much later.
Incorrect. The Sassanid Persians took eastern Mesopotamia in 226 AD, not 539 BC.
Incorrect. The Neo-Assyrian Empire asserted control from 900 to 612 BC, before 539 BC.

Incorrect. The article does not identify Turks as descendants of Ancient Sumerians.
